name: Misfits and Hooligans
description: At five minutes and forty-nine seconds, 'Misfits and Hooligans' is That Boy Hi Hat's longest record on Spotify — and it earns every second. An Idol or Icon (2021) standout, the track is a sprawling underground hip hop statement built for the outsiders: hard-hitting drums, a bass line that rolls rather than stabs, and a hook designed to be shouted back. That Boy Hi Hat writes the whole thing like a manifesto for the kids who never fit the room, and the length becomes a feature — verses stack into verses, the beat breathes, and the defiant energy compounds rather than dissipates. There's an anthemic quality to it that the catalog's darker cuts don't chase: this is hype as community-building, the sound of a crowd finding each other. The post trap architecture keeps it modern — crisp hi-hats, layered low end — but the spirit is older than that, closer to the raw collectivism of early underground rap crews. For a catalog that leans atmospheric and nocturnal, 'Misfits and Hooligans' is That Boy Hi Hat at his most communal: dangerous in intent, inclusive in invitation. It plays like a set-closer even on record, and it's the clearest evidence that his songwriting scales to ambition when the canvas is wide.
